summary.text: Mohenjo-daro is an archaeological site in Larkana District, Sindh, Pakistan, built around 2500 BCE as one of the largest settlements of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
With an estimated population of at least 40,000, it prospered for several centuries before it was abandoned by about 1700 BCE.
The city had a planned layout of rectilinear buildings on a grid, mostly of fired and mortared brick, with covered drains lining the major streets.

facts.label: Name meaning
facts.value: Mound of the Dead, in Sindhi

facts.label: Great Bath
facts.value: A brick-built pool 12 m long, 7 m wide, 2.4 m deep

items.prompt: A visitor learns the site's modern name in Sindhi. What does it mean?

options.label: City of the Cockerel
Place of Great Waters
City of the Great Bath
Mound of the Dead

items.explain: Mohenjo-daro, the modern name for the site, has been interpreted as Mound of the Dead in Sindhi.

items.prompt: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer found no evidence of grain in the building Wheeler called the Great Granary. What does he suggest instead?

options.label: Its function is uncertain, so Great Hall is a better name
It stored grain until the city was abandoned
It was a hall built to house the city's rulers
It was a bathing pool for the whole population

items.explain: Kenoyer noted the complete lack of evidence for grain, arguing that it might be better termed a Great Hall of uncertain function.

items.prompt: The raised mud-brick mound called the Citadel at Mohenjo-daro held which kinds of buildings?

options.label: Only private houses belonging to ordinary families
Public baths, a large residence and two assembly halls
The central marketplace with its large public well
Workshops and drains serving the whole lower city

items.explain: The Citadel is known to have supported public baths, a large residential structure designed to house about 5,000 citizens, and two large assembly halls.

items.prompt: What do the city's size and its public buildings and facilities suggest about its society?

options.label: A high level of social organisation
A loose camp with no shared planning
A festival site used only briefly
Rule by a single foreign king

items.explain: The sheer size of the city, and its provision of public buildings and facilities, suggests a high level of social organisation.

items.prompt: Digging at Mohenjo-daro has been banned since 1965, apart from salvage and conservation projects. What was the reason?

options.label: Nothing more remained to be found
The site proved much smaller than thought
Floods from the Indus had covered the ruins
Weathering was damaging the exposed structures

items.explain: After 1965 excavations were banned due to weathering damage to the exposed structures.

items.prompt: How did Mohenjo-daro deal with waste water from its houses?

options.label: It was piped into one central well
It was collected in the Great Bath
It was channeled to covered drains lining the major streets
It was left to run through the courtyards

items.explain: Waste water was channeled to covered drains that lined the major streets.
